## Description

Two kinds of switch (owner decision 15 Nov 2026, plan on issue #774). The clinic's own switch (MDV-P0-028) stays with the practice owner. A new Medvya switch per feature and country, set from the platform console page Features, releases a feature in stages: Off, Internal (Medvya's own test organisations), Beta (named organisations), Percentage, Everyone. A feature is on in a clinic only when the Medvya switch reaches that organisation and, where the feature has one, the clinic's switch is on; off means its endpoints answer 404 and the clinic app hides it. One feature list in code (key, clinical yes/no, countries, clinic switch, always on) replaces the copies of the keys. Keys that existed before start released to Everyone, so nothing disappears for clinics; a new key starts Off. Patient record, allergies, prescription signing, audit log and data export are always on and locked. A one-click 'turn off for all' hides a feature in every country without deleting data. A clinical feature cannot reach Everyone until a clinical sign-off is recorded. Plans decide who is entitled (MDV-P5-042, later); flags decide what is on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given a clinical flag, when is moved to everyone without sign-off, then the change is refused.
- [ ] **AC2.** Given the kill switch, when is used, then the feature disappears for all tenants and no data is deleted.
- [ ] **AC3.** Given a flag change, when is made, then it is audited with a reason.
- [ ] **AC4.** Given the Medvya switch is off for a feature, when a clinic with its own switch on calls the feature, then the endpoint answers 404 and the clinic app hides it.
- [ ] **AC5.** Given a support, finance or reviewer console member, when they change a release, then the server refuses it (403); only owner and operations change releases.
- [ ] **AC6.** Given an always-on feature, when anyone tries to switch it off, then the change is refused.

## Notes / open questions

- Scope (ADR-016 (docs/adr/ADR-016-organisation-onboarding-and-approval.md)): rollout targets are organisations, and optionally one location of an organisation, never a single doctor.
- Country data stays in country (ADR-003): the Medvya release lives in each country's clinic database (a non-tenant table), read by the clinic API with a cache of at most 60 s. The console writes it through a narrow database login per country (medvya_features: that one table, nothing else), following the medvya_review pattern of ADR-014; the clinic application may read it but not change it.
- Plan entitlements are not part of this ticket; MDV-P5-042 adds them to the same check.

## Definition of Done

All acceptance criteria above, **plus** the cross-cutting X1–X8 checklist in [docs/05-delivery](../../README.md#definition-of-done-every-ticket).
